problem: Earlier EQA methods train exploration and QA modules from scratch in mostly synthetic scenes and handle only simple templated questions (e.g., object colour). Plugging an off-the-shelf VLM into EQA raises two problems: the VLM has no memory or map to plan exploration over time, and its miscalibrated confidence makes the robot stop too early or explore too long.
motivation: VLMs can reason semantically about where relevant information is likely to be (e.g., going through a door to reach a bedroom) and can answer open-ended questions. Two observations drive the work: raw VLM softmax scores are over- or under-confident, and a VLM gives confident but biased answers even when looking at irrelevant views such as a blank wall. So efficient exploration needs both an external semantic memory that guides where to go and a calibrated rule for when to stop.
key_idea: Store the VLM's visual-prompting scores for where to explore in an external semantic map that weights frontier-based exploration, and use multi-step conformal prediction on relevance-weighted answer confidences so the robot stops once the calibrated answer set shrinks to one option.
insight: Both semantic cues are needed. In the Fig. 7b ablation, dropping GSV gives higher early success but the planner becomes myopic and plateaus, while dropping LSV lowers efficiency overall; either ablation performs on par with or worse than plain FBE. Too high a temperature (τ=5) over-trusts VLM reasoning and hurts later performance. For stopping, entropy stops prematurely because the VLM is confidently wrong on irrelevant views; relevance-gating fixes this but over-explores. Conformal prediction on the product Rel·(f_y−1), taking the per-episode minimum and intersecting per-step sets, reaches 58% SR with about 71% of the maximum steps versus 85% for Relevance, with the largest gains at high target success. By category, the gains appear mainly in Count and Existence questions, where the question names a location; there is no gain on Identification. Overall SR (about 60%) is limited mainly by VLM answering errors, not by exploration.
method: Exploration map: 3D TSDF voxel fusion from depth images, projected to a 2D map of free/occupied (free if all voxels up to 1.5 m are empty) and explored/unexplored. Only the central 50% of HFOV and lower 50% of VFOV mark voxels as explored, giving finer-grained exploration.

Local Semantic Value (LSV): project the current view's free space onto the map, pick |P|=3 points by farthest point sampling, label them A/B/C on the RGB image (visual prompting), and use the VLM's normalized probability over the letters as a per-point value.

Global Semantic Value (GSV): a yes/no prompt asking whether any area in the view is worth exploring for the question, scored by normalized P('Yes'). Combined as SV_p = exp(τ_LSV·LSV_p + τ_GSV·GSV_p) and Gaussian-smoothed into the semantic map.

Semantic-value-weighted frontier exploration: sample the next frontier with weight w_p = exp(τ_SV·SV_p + τ_SV,Normal·SV_p,normal), where SV_p,normal averages SV within d_SV = 3 m along the frontier normal; the planner then moves to a pose at most 3 m away.

Relevance-weighted confidence: Rel(x) is the normalized P('Yes') for 'can this view answer the question'; the score is ρ_y = Rel(x)(f_y(x) − 1), where f_y is the VLM's softmax over answer choices A–D.

Multi-step conformal prediction (following KnowNo): the episode score is min_t ρ_y^t, and threshold q̂ is calibrated on 300 scenarios for coverage 1−ε. At test time the per-step sets C^t are intersected and the robot stops when one answer remains; if the horizon is reached or the set is empty, it answers argmax f_y at the step with the highest Rel.

HM-EQA dataset: 500 multiple-choice questions over 267 HM3D scenes, generated by GPT4-V from 12 random views plus 3 hand-written examples, then manually filtered. Categories: Identification 16.2%, Counting 16.0%, Existence 21.6%, State 20.2%, Location 26.0%. Step budget T = 3·sqrt(scene area).

setting.backbone: Prismatic VLM (frozen, used via token probabilities); variants with LLaVA 1.6 and GPT4-V (official API with logprobs); one variant with Prismatic fine-tuned for QA
setting.training_data: none (training-free); conformal calibration uses 300 HM-EQA scenarios; the fine-tuned variant fine-tunes Prismatic for QA on 300 HM-EQA scenarios
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (single camera, 120° HFOV / 105° VFOV in sim) + pose (perfect odometry in sim, localization on real robot)
setting.action_space: sampled frontier waypoints/poses (≤3 m per step) executed by a collision-free planner; a stop/answer decision
setting.privileged: perfect odometry/GT pose in simulation; otherwise none

numbers_note: The paper has no results tables. The main exploration and stopping comparisons (Ours vs FBE, CLIP-FBE, No-LSV, No-GSV, temperature sweep, Entropy, Relevance) appear only as curves of normalized time step vs success rate (Figs. 7, 9), with per-category and per-scene-size breakdowns also only in figures. Numbers stated in the text: 58.4% SR at max steps (Prismatic); a view-orientation variant at 59.3%; for stopping, to reach 58% SR 'our method takes about 71% of the maximum time steps while Relevance takes 85%' (approximate, on the 200-scenario CP test split). Hardware: 6 Fetch scenarios, Ours 4/6 correct (same as Relevance, fewer steps). No numbers are reported for the FBE or CLIP-FBE baselines.
results: On HM-EQA (500 scenarios), VLM-guided semantic exploration reaches a given success rate in fewer steps than FBE and CLIP-FBE; the gap is largest at 20-30% of the step budget, and final SR is 58.4% with Prismatic, 65.3% with LLaVA 1.6 and 73.9% with GPT4-V. Conformal-prediction stopping beats Entropy by a wide margin and reaches 58% SR with about 71% of the maximum steps versus about 85% for relevance-threshold stopping. On a real Fetch robot (6 scenarios) it matches Relevance at 4/6 correct while stopping earlier. Fine-tuning the VLM on 300 scenarios raises SR from 56.2% to 68.1% on the 200 held-out scenarios.
limitations: The semantic value ignores view orientation, and the VLM reasons over one image at a time with no multi-view memory; overall SR (about 60%) is bounded by VLM answering errors even when the relevant object is in view.
The method needs token log-probabilities, which rules out closed models without logprobs (e.g., GPT4-V preview), and it assumes multiple-choice questions.

The conformal guarantee assumes calibration and test scenarios are i.i.d.; 300 labeled calibration episodes are needed, and simulation assumes perfect odometry. Exploration is heuristic and sensitive to the temperature τ.
